title: VENAT · native venous statistical fields

scalar.interpretation: A source-computed mean partial-volume field, not the probability of a named vessel or an individual segmentation.
scalar.derivation: Repeated 7 T QSM vessel estimates were transformed and aggregated by the source authors. The project retains their original field.
scalar.reference: Huck et al. (2019), High resolution atlas of the venous brain vasculature from 7 T quantitative susceptibility maps. doi:10.1007/s00429-019-01919-4. Methods: Vascular atlas and Density Map. Data: doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7205960.v4.

scalar.interpretation: Spatial variability of the source estimates includes anatomy, measurement and source processing effects; it is not a named variant prevalence.
scalar.derivation: Author-supplied standard deviation of venous partial-volume estimates in the supplied atlas grid.
scalar.reference: Huck et al. (2019), High resolution atlas of the venous brain vasculature from 7 T quantitative susceptibility maps. doi:10.1007/s00429-019-01919-4. Methods: Vascular atlas and Density Map. Data: doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7205960.v4.

scalar.statistic: Population mean of repeated detection fractions
scalar.interpretation: A source detection-frequency field, not direct lumen volume or the frequency of an anatomical variant.
scalar.derivation: The authors binarized positive vessel probabilities, averaged repeated observations, retained detections at two or more time points, then averaged participant maps.
scalar.reference: Huck et al. (2019), High resolution atlas of the venous brain vasculature from 7 T quantitative susceptibility maps. doi:10.1007/s00429-019-01919-4. Methods: Vascular atlas and Density Map. Data: doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7205960.v4.

scalar.interpretation: Source-computed diameter estimates on the supplied vascular skeleton; zeros outside that support are not zero-diameter vessels.
scalar.derivation: Author estimates and native atlas skeleton support are retained. No new vessel fitting or centerline extraction is performed.
scalar.reference: Huck et al. (2019), High resolution atlas of the venous brain vasculature from 7 T quantitative susceptibility maps. doi:10.1007/s00429-019-01919-4. Methods: Vascular atlas and Density Map. Data: doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7205960.v4.

scalar.statistic: Population standard deviation on source skeleton
scalar.interpretation: Source variability of diameter estimates on atlas support, not an uncertainty bound for an individual vessel.
scalar.derivation: Author-supplied standard deviation on the supplied skeleton support.
scalar.reference: Huck et al. (2019), High resolution atlas of the venous brain vasculature from 7 T quantitative susceptibility maps. doi:10.1007/s00429-019-01919-4. Methods: Vascular atlas and Density Map. Data: doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7205960.v4.

scalar.interpretation: Source-computed curvature of skeleton estimates; not direct observation of a named branch boundary.
scalar.derivation: Author-supplied curvature estimates and source skeleton support are retained without project smoothing.
scalar.reference: Huck et al. (2019), High resolution atlas of the venous brain vasculature from 7 T quantitative susceptibility maps. doi:10.1007/s00429-019-01919-4. Methods: Vascular atlas and Density Map. Data: doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7205960.v4.

scalar.statistic: Population standard deviation on source skeleton
scalar.interpretation: Variability of source curvature estimates; zeros outside skeleton support carry no individual anatomical interpretation.
scalar.derivation: Author-supplied standard deviation on the supplied skeleton support.
scalar.reference: Huck et al. (2019), High resolution atlas of the venous brain vasculature from 7 T quantitative susceptibility maps. doi:10.1007/s00429-019-01919-4. Methods: Vascular atlas and Density Map. Data: doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7205960.v4.

space.name: VENAT v4 native atlas grid
space.reference: Original NIfTI qform, code 1, millimeter units. The publisher describes MNI152 atlas space.
space.correspondence: Seven fields share the exact supplied grid. No reference MRI accompanies this release. A shared MNI name does not validate overlay with another dataset; cross-source browsing remains independent.

sources.title: VENAT · twenty healthy participants with repeated 7 T QSM
sources.citation: Huck et al. (2019), High resolution atlas of the venous brain vasculature from 7 T quantitative susceptibility maps. doi:10.1007/s00429-019-01919-4. Methods: Vascular atlas and Density Map. Data: doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7205960.v4.

scope_notes: The original source describes twenty healthy young adults. These population estimates cannot establish an individual venous branch identity or named normal-variant prevalence.

The authors excluded deep gray matter from venous estimation because of confounding susceptibility. Mask erosion also limits superficial sinus coverage. Absence of signal is not evidence of absent anatomy.
All source NIfTI bytes, native grid, units and field values are retained. Display contrast and 3D intensity rendering do not create segmented boundaries.
Diameter and curvature apply to the supplied source skeleton support. Background zeros do not describe zero diameter or curvature of individual vessels.
Two acquired torsion files are retained in source storage but omitted from browsing until their interpretation and units are reconciled with the final publication.
acquisition: Run neuroimage acquire venat --data-root <data-root>. Existing verified source files are reused without extraction.
